1.

By way of this petition, the petitioner has challenged the order dated 06.03.2024 passed by the Sub-Divisional Officer (Revenue), Giroud, District Baloudabazar, Bhatapara, whereby the petitioner,
who was officiating Sarpanch of Gram Panchayat Kumhari, Tahshil- Tundra, District- Baloda Bazar,
Bhatapara has been placed under suspension Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:12003 according to the provisions of Section 39 (1)(b) of Chhattisgarh Panchayat Raj Adhiniyam, 1993 (henceforth "Adhiniyam, 1993").
2.
The facts of the present case are that the petitioner was elected as Surpanch of Gram Panchayat Kumhari in the year 2020.

On 14.09.2021, Devnath and two other persons namely, Rajesh Sahu and Shankar Patel, who are residents of the same Gram Panchayat, moved an application under Section 40 of the Adhiniyam, 1993 making certain allegations with regard to financial irregularities before the Sub- Divisional Officer (Revenue)/ Prescribed Officer, Kasdol, District Baloda Bazar-Bhatapara.

sentences.text: The concerned SDO (R), who is the prescribed authority, initiated the proceeding.
An enquiry was conducted and its report was submitted on 23.11.2021.
According to said report, allegations made against the petitioner were found false and fabricated.

Thereafter, the complainants filed an appeal before the Collector, Balodabazar - Bhatapara against the order dated 30.11.2021 passed by the concerned SDO (R), whereby the proceedings pending against the petitioner were dropped.

The Collector, vide its order dated 19.12.2022 remitted back the matter to the Sub Divisional Officer (Revenue), Kasdol to decide it afresh after affording a due opportunity of hearing to the complainants.

The SDO (R), pursuant to the order passed by the Collector, again initiated proceedings under Section 40 of the Adhiniyam, 1993 against the petitioner and while exercising its power under Section 39(1)(b) of Adhiniyam, 1993 placed the petitioner under suspension vide order dated 06.03.2024, which is under challenge.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the complainants have no right to challenge the order passed by the Sub-Divisional Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:12003 Officer (Revenue) in favour of the petitioner.

He would further submit that in the enquiry initiated against the petitioner,
she was exonerated and the proceedings pending before the Sub-Divisional Officer (Revenue) were dropped therefore, no order of suspension would have been passed by the SDO (R) against the petitioner.

4. In support thereof, he placed reliance on the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Ravi Yashwant Bhoi Vs. Collector reported in 2012 (4) SCC 407 and would submit that the complainant cannot be a party to the lis and under the garb of being a necessary party, a person cannot be permitted to make a case as that of general public interest.

sentences.text:
The relevant paragraphs 58, 59 and 60 are reproduced herein below:-
58.
Shri Chintaman Raghunath Gharat, Ex-President was the complainant, thus, at the most, he could lead the evidence as a witness.
He could not claim the status of an adversial litigant.
The complainant cannot be the party to the lis.
A legal right is an averment of entitlement arising out of law.
In fact, it is a benefit conferred upon a person by the rule of law.
Thus, a person who uffers from legal injury can only challenge the act or omission.

There may be some harm or loss that may not be wrongful in the eyes of law because it may not result in injury to a legal right or legally protected interest of the complainant but juridically harm of this description is called damnum sine injuria.
59. The complainant has to establish that he has been deprived of or denied of a legal right and he has sustained injury to any legally protected interest.
In case he has no legal peg for a justiciable claim to hang on, he cannot be heard as a party in a lis.
A fanciful or sentimental grievance may not be sufficient to confer a locus standi to sue upon the individual.
There must be injuria or a legal grievance which can be appreciated and not a stat pro ratione valuntas reasons i.e. a claim devoid of reasons.
60. Under the garb of being necessary party, a person cannot be permitted to make a case as that of general public interest.

5. On the other hand, learned counsels appearing for the respondents would submit that the Sub-Divisional Officer (Revenue) has initiated a proceeding under Section 40 of the Adhiniyam,
1993 in pursuance of the order passed by the Collector, Baloda Bazar - Bhatapara dated 19.12.2022 and the petitioner has not challenged the very order in this petition.
They would further submit that the order dated 19.12.2022 has already been challenged by the petitioner before the Commissioner by way of filing a revision which is still pending.
They would also submit that the matter of the petitioner with regard to her suspension has been referred to the State Government according to the provisions of Section 39(2) of the Adhiniyam, 1993.

They would further contend that an enquiry is pending against the petitioner before the Sub-Divisional Officer and while exercising power under Section 39(1)(b) of the Adhiniyam, 1993, the SDO (R), who is the prescribed authority, may place the office bearer under suspension, therefore the concerned SDO (R) is justified in passing the order impugned and the instant petition deserves to be dismissed.
6. I have heard learned counsel appearing for the parties and perused the documents available on the record.

7. Section 39 of the Adhiniyam, 1993 reads as under:-
39. Suspension of office-bearer of Panchayat.

- (1) The prescribed authority may suspend from office any-office bearer,-

Protection of Civil Rights and Prevention of Corruption; or [(b) on whom, show cause notice along with charge-sheet under this Act, has been served for removal from office.]

Provided further that where the office of Sarpanch or President is reserved for a woman belonging to Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes or Other Backward Classes and there is no other woman member of the Panchayat belonging, to that category who can be elected to officiate as Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:12003 Sarpanch or President, as the case may be, any other woman member belonging to the other reserved categories, may be elected to officiate as Sarpanch or President as the case may be.

(4) A person who has been suspended under sub-section (1) shall also forthwith stand suspended from the office of member or office-bearer of any other Panchayat of which he is a member or office-bearer.
Such person shall also be disqualified for being elected under the Act during his suspension.

8. From a bare perusal of Section 39 of the Adhiniyam, it is quite vivid that the prescribed authority/SDO (R) while exercising power may place an office bearer under suspension, if against such office bearer charges have been framed in any criminal proceeding mentioned in Section 39(A)
of the Adhiniyam, 1993 or on whom show cause notice along with the said charge-sheet under this act has been served for removal from the office.
9. In the present case, earlier the charge sheet along with the show cause notice was issued to the petitioner and an enquiry was conducted.

In the enquiry, nothing was found proved against the petitioner, therefore, the proceeding initiated against the petitioner under Section 40 of the Adhiniyam, 1993 was dropped, but the said order was challenged by the complainant before the Collector and the concerned Collector vide its order dated 19.12.2022 remitted back the matter to decide it afresh after affording due opportunity of hearing to the complainants.

10. The subsequent proceeding was initiated by the SDO (R) pursuant to the order passed by the Collector on 19.12.2022, but the very order has not been challenged by the petitioner for the reasons best known to her.

11. The order passed by the Sub-Divisional Officer (Revenue) has been referred to the State Government according to provisions of Section Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:12003 39(2) of the Adhiniyam, 1993 for confirmation and if it is not confirmed within a period of 90 days, it would be deemed to have vacated.

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Ravi Yashwant Bhoi (supra) observed and held that the complainants cannot claim the status of an adversarial litigant and cannot be a party to the lis.
It is further held that the complainant has to establish that he has been deprived of or denied a legal right and he has sustained injury to any legally protected interest.
It is further held that under the garb of being a necessary party, a person cannot be permitted to make a case as that of general public interest.

13. In the instant case, the complainants before the Collector established that they had been deprived of their legal right and after taking into consideration the submissions made by the complainants before the Collector, the matter was remitted back to the SDO (R) to hear it afresh after affording the due opportunity of hearing and at the same time, the petitioner has not challenged the order passed by the Collector before this Court and the same is under challenge before the Commissioner in a revision.
14. Taking into consideration the above-discussed facts and provisions of law, in the considered opinion of this Court, no case is made out calling for any interference.
15. As a result, this petition fails and is hereby dismissed.
No costs.
